framing_note: Treat the trending Gaia episode as a trend signal only, not as evidence. Scholarly sources support studying sound in ancient Egyptian worship spaces and musical practice; they do not establish that sound frequencies built the pyramids or that ancient Egyptians possessed a modern acoustic/quantum theory.

sources.title: Assessing the Acoustics of an Ancient Egyptian temple
sources.review_anchor: Abstract; sections II–IV; measurement campaign and post-processing
sources.relevance: Reports an acoustic measurement campaign at the Dendera temple using a spherical microphone array and room impulse responses. It notes the temple's sound-related religious context.
sources.limitations: The paper says no text has been found showing that acoustical theory governed temple design; whether properties were intentional or incidental remains debated.

sources.title: The Sound of Ancient Egypt – Acoustics and Volume Measurements
sources.review_anchor: Full article pp. 13–33; methods and measurements of replica instruments
sources.relevance: Discusses acoustic conditions at ancient Egyptian performance venues and measurements of replicas of ancient Egyptian musical instruments.
sources.limitations: Replica measurements and venue comparisons do not establish supernatural effects or a hidden engineering technology.

sources.title: The Rattles from Tell el-Farcha: Acoustic Research with the Use of Numerical Sound Reconstruction
sources.publication: Studies in Ancient Art and Civilization 25, 7–29
sources.review_anchor: Full paper pp. 7–29; acoustic analysis and numerical reconstruction
sources.relevance: Uses sound analysis and numerical reconstruction to study ancient Egyptian clay rattles and explore aspects of past soundscapes.
sources.limitations: Reconstruction is a research method, not a recording of the exact sound heard in antiquity.

candidate_claims.text: A 2021 study measured acoustic properties in the Dendera temple using a spherical microphone array and room-impulse-response analysis.

The Dendera acoustics study says there is no known ancient Egyptian text demonstrating that a formal acoustic theory governed temple design; intentional design versus incidental acoustics remains debated.
Researchers have measured replicas of ancient Egyptian musical instruments and used archaeological, textual, and iconographic evidence to study ancient performance sound.
Researchers have used acoustic analysis and numerical sound reconstruction to investigate ancient Egyptian clay rattles from Tell el-Farcha.

unsupported_claims: Ancient Egyptians used sound frequencies to build the pyramids.
Ancient Egyptian temples were proven to be designed as acoustic amplifiers for supernatural energy.
Sound or vibration can be presented as a proven quantum healing technology based on these archaeological studies.
reviewer_instructions: Inspect the original paper and exact methods/results before approval.
Keep the Dendera temple's Ptolemaic/Roman-era context separate from Old Kingdom pyramid construction.
Distinguish measured acoustics, reconstructed sounds, and interpretations of ritual experience.
Mark claims about intentional acoustic design as DEBATED unless the paper establishes them directly.
No claim enters the evidence ledger until a human reviewer records source approval and an exact reference.
